samples.summary: A group whose only children are dropped images now serializes as a childless `<p:grpSp>`
samples.evidence: `elementToXml` returns `''` for an image whose rId resolved to `null` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:65). `groupToXml` builds its children with `data.children.map(...).join('')` and unconditionally wraps them (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:115-117), so a group element containing only image children whose fetch failed emits `<p:grpSp>` with `nvGrpSpPr`/`grpSpPr` and no shape children. An empty group shape tree is not what the writer previously could produce (the old resolver threw instead), and PowerPoint commonly reports such a part as needing repair. The fix belongs in `groupToXml` (skip a group that serialized no children) rather than at the new `null` return.

samples.summary: The widened try in `collectAndEmbedImages` makes `onImageError` swallow decode/embed failures too, not just fetch failures — unlike the DOCX and PPTX paths
samples.evidence: In packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts the try now spans `fetcher(src)`, `blob.arrayBuffer()`, the mime sniff and `embedPng`/`embedJpg`/`embedAsPng` (lines 81-101). `embedAsPng` is documented as browser-only — "Node/jsdom callers that hit a non-PNG/JPEG src will get a clear error" (same file, lines ~36-42) — so a CLI `docs export --format pdf` of a document containing a WebP/GIF image, or corrupt bytes, now drops the image with a stderr warning where it previously failed loudly. The two sibling exporters kept the format step outside the tolerant region: `deriveExt(blob)` runs after the catch in packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:479, and `extFromMime(fetched.mime)` after the catch in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:184, so the same document behaves differently per format.

samples.summary: The CLI design doc's primary error table still describes the pre-`forwardUpstreamError` mechanism
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:911 still lists "HTTP 400 / 404 / 409, bad flags, type mismatch | command-specific or `ERROR` | 1", and the prose at docs/design/cli.md:919-924 still describes the two-path scheme ("`throw httpError(status)` where the CLI writes the message, and `process.exitCode = exitCodeForStatus(status)` on the `content`/`export` paths"). After this change a non-envelope 400/404 reports `HTTP_ERROR` via `forwardUpstreamError` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:261,321) and no command uses the old two-path split, so the earlier table contradicts the newer one at docs/design/cli.md:1492. cli.md is a top-level design doc whose prose is not checked by any lane, only its backticked paths.

samples.summary: Design-doc row for "download returned 2xx with no bytes" still promises the backend body / bare `HTTP_ERROR` envelope
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:1500 documents the message column as "(backend body, else `{ error: { code: \"HTTP_ERROR\" } }`)". The new code emits a fixed synthesized message instead — `HTTP ${res.status} carried no file content for document ${docId}` (packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:86-88) — and deliberately never forwards the body on that branch, so the documented shape no longer matches what an agent will read.

samples.summary: Design-doc row saying a refused image `src` exits 1 with `IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED` now only holds for the non-export paths
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:1498 lists "Image `src` the CLI refuses to dereference | 1 | IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED" as an unqualified row, but every CLI export path now passes `reportSkippedImage` (packages/cli/src/docs/pdf-export.ts:118, packages/cli/src/docs/docx-export.ts:39-42, packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:22), so `docs export` / `slides export` exit 0 with a stderr warning. Only the `docs content --inline-images` fetcher still surfaces that code and exit class, which the row does not say. The later section at docs/design/cli.md:1573 states the new behaviour, leaving the matrix row internally contradictory.

samples.summary: `docs export --pages` runs the PDF export twice, so each skipped image is now reported twice on stderr
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:283 renders the full PDF to count pages and packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:292 renders it again with the page range; both now pass `onImageError: reportSkippedImage` via `exportPdf` (packages/cli/src/docs/pdf-export.ts:118), so every unreachable/refused image produces two identical `Skipping image …` lines on the stderr an agent parses.

finding.summary: A group whose only children are dropped images now serializes as a childless `<p:grpSp>`
finding.evidence: `elementToXml` returns `''` for an image whose rId resolved to `null` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:65). `groupToXml` builds its children with `data.children.map(...).join('')` and unconditionally wraps them (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:115-117), so a group element containing only image children whose fetch failed emits `<p:grpSp>` with `nvGrpSpPr`/`grpSpPr` and no shape children. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed. group.ts:62-67 returns '' for an image whose rId resolves to null, and groupToXml at group.ts:115-117 joins child XML and wraps it unconditionally, so a group whose children all serialize empty emits <p:grpSp> with only nvGrpSpPr/grpSpPr. The null branch is reachable from the public entry point: index.ts:305-321 returns null whenever the src is missing from srcToMediaPath, which occurs when fetchImage throws and onImageError is supplied (index.ts:172-187). No guard prunes such elements before serialization (slide.ts:157, index.ts:357). Two mitigating facts exist but neither refutes: the chart case (group.ts:74-77) already made an empty group producible before this change (pre-existing is still a defect under this rubric), and the importer explicitly tolerates empty groups (import/pptx/shape.ts:219-229), so the in-repo round-trip does not break. The impact claim (PowerPoint repair prompt on a childless grpSp) is empirical and cannot be verified from the repository, so I cannot name a counterexample ground. Consumer of a changed return contract left unupdated - stays in the gate.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding is not a claim about a code location — it is the panel's own synthetic record that a lens never produced a verdict. The quoted text is generated verbatim by poolExhaustedError (scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-636, message at :632) and wrapped by lensFailureSummary's non-infra branch (scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1690-1695); the persisted artifact for the security lens shows exactly this summary (.agent-review/security/verdict.json:75, .agent-review/security/summary.md:5). With no file or symbol asserted, there is nothing I can show to be absent, unreachable, or mis-quoted, so no refutation ground applies. Moreover the repository deliberately treats this string as blocking: review-panel.mjs:1684-1688 states the non-infra no-verdict path "IS an ordinary fail-closed blocker" (in contrast to the "Review could not run" infra prefix, which must never be re-checked as a code finding), and poolExhaustedError sets no `infra` flag (ask.mjs:634-635), so it routes to that blocking branch by construction. rounds.mjs:561-565 only exempts such summaries from stall detection, not from the gate. Refuting would let a lens that never executed pass the merge gate silently — the exact failure the fail-closed design prevents (see the open task docs/tasks/active/20260820-fixer-live-credential-todo.md:8). Under confirm-on-doubt, it stays.
